name: Screened twisted pair
summary: Two conductors drawn twisted together inside a screen outline, as used for noise-sensitive signal and communication pairs.
description: The screened twisted pair combines two separate protections against interference. Twisting cancels magnetically induced voltage between the two cores, and the screen intercepts capacitive coupling from nearby power conductors. The form is typical for RS-485 links, 4 to 20 mA loops in noisy plant and resolver or encoder feedback pairs.

On a drawing each screened pair should be identifiable in the core allocation, because a multipair cable may contain several of them plus an overall screen. The symbol does not tell you the characteristic impedance or twist rate, which matter for data networks and must come from the cable specification.
readingNotes: Confirm the pair belongs to the circuit it is drawn on, not split across two circuits.
Check how the pair screen is terminated relative to any overall screen.
drawingChecklist: Allocate both cores of the pair to one signal circuit.
Record cable impedance for data circuits.
distinction: A screened twisted pair adds a shield; the plain twisted-pair indication shows twisting only and no screen.
